:: J U D G M E N T :
:
Petitioners have filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Giri in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 29.08.2021 at about 5.30 p.m., Giri was proceeding as a pillion rider on the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 and the said vehicle was reached near Canara Bank, on Madanapalli-Palamaner road, at that point of time, the rider of said motor cycle drove the vehicle in a rash or negligent manner, endangering to human life with high speed.
Due to excess speed, the rider of motor cycle lost control over the vehicle and caused the accident.
As a result Giri and the rider of offending vehicle fell down from the motor cycle and the Giri sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately Giri was shifted to Government Hospital, Palamaner and thereafter for better treatment, he was shifted to SVIMS (Ruya) Hospital, Tirupati.
In-spite of better treatment, Giri succumbed to injuries in the hospital.
The petitioners are the parents of the deceased.
Due to death of deceased Giri, they have put to untold misery and mental agony.
The deceased was aged 19 years and he was doing stone cutting work and earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
The deceased was only bread earner of the family and the petitioners were depending on the earning of the deceased.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners are facing extreme difficulty to eke out their livelihood.

The accident was occurred only due to rash or negligent riding of the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 and in this regard Gangavaram police have registered the case against the rider of above said vehicle.
The 1 st respondent is the RC owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the Motorcycle bearing Venkatasu vs S. Subbamma on 7 January, 2025

2 Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252.
With these averments petitioners prays to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st respondent remained absent, hence she has been placed Ex- parte.
The 2nd respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the 2 nd respondent/Insurance company are as hereunder:
The respondent No.1 has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) of M.V. Act, as she has not furnished any documents with respect to offending vehicle.
Further, the police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of M.V.
Act.
The insured has knowingly entrusted the offending vehicle to the rider, who had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle.
Hence, she has breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
The police have filed charge sheet against the rider of motor cycle under Sec.3(a) and Sec.181 of M.V. Act.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its validity with respect to vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 and contended that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, valid and effective driving licence of the rider of vehicle.
The offending vehicle was not involved in the accident and caused the accident.
The petitioners in collusion with the police have created false records and implicated the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 to get compensation.
The accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself and not due to negligent act of rider of the offending vehicle.
This respondent denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
With these averments, the 2nd respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1. Whether petitioners prove that, Giri was died on 29.08.2021 due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of rider of motor cycle vehicle bearing Registration No.AP-39-S-6252 as stated in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that, rider of the motor cycle has no valid and effective DL?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
5. What order or award?

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1:-

It is the case of the petitioners that, deceased Giri was proceeding as a pillion rider on the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 and the said vehicle was reached near Canara Bank, on Madanapalli-Palamaner road, at that point of time, the rider of said motor cycle drove the vehicle in a rash or negligent manner, endangering to human life with high speed.
Due to excess speed, the rider of motor cycle lost control over the vehicle and caused the accident.
As a result deceased Giri fell down from the motor cycle and he has sustained grievous injuries.
In-spite of better treatment, Giri succumbed to injuries in the hospital.

In order to prove her contention, the 2 nd petitioner, who is the mother of deceased has examined as P.W.1 and filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and reiterated the averments made in the petition.
She also produced 12 documents, which are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
It is relevant to note that, respondent No.2 has not disputed the accident.

In order to answer Issue No.1, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4,
Ex.P.2(a) and Ex.P.8 for discussion.
Ex . P.1
is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.177/2021.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of complaint.
Ex. P.2(a) is the English translated copy of complaint.
Ex . P.3
is the true copy of postmortem report.
Ex . P.4
is the true copy of charge sheet.
Ex. P.8
is the notarized copy of death certificate of deceased Giri.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.4, it is crystal clear that, the police have filed charge sheet against the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252.
9.
Admittedly, there is no dispute with regard to death of Giri in a road accident occurred on 29.08.2021 .
According to the respondent No.2, the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident and caused the accident.
The petitioners in collusion with the police have created false records and implicated the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 to get compensation.
The accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself and not due to negligent act of rider of the offending vehicle.
In order to prove the said contention, the 2 nd respondent has not placed any oral or documentary evidence.

sentences.text: At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

11. Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaju and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
12.
Now, the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 or not?
In order to answer this aspect, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the rider of Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.4.

It is relevant to note that, though the respondent No.2 has contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, however, in order to substantiate the same, the 2nd respondent has not placed any material before this Tribunal.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 by its rider.
The above referred decisions are squarely applicable to the case on hand.
In the instant case, it is relevant to note that, the respondent No.2-Insurance company has not examined the rider of offending vehicle.

At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider, the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S- 6252 ride the same in a rash or negligent manner and lost control over the said vehicle and capsized the motor cycle on the road.
Due to the said impact, the deceased Giri sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries on 01.09.2021 while taking treatment in the hospital.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that rider of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP- 39-S-6252 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE No.2:- This issue with respect to age and income of the deceased.
Age:- According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 19 years as on the date of accident.
In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age of the deceased.
In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, which is marked as Ex.P.5.
On careful perusal of said document, it reveals that, the year of birth of deceased is mentioned as 2003.
The accident was occurred on 29.08.2021.
Therefore, age of the deceased is considered as 18 years at the time of accident.

sentences.text: Income of the deceased:- According to the petitioners, the deceased was doing stone cutting work and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, respondent No.2 has disputed the avocation and income of deceased.
In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has not produced the documents.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another,

wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
15. In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.

As such in the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2021 is Rs.15,000/- per month.
In the instant case, accident was occurred in the year 2021.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.3:-

According to respondent No.2, the insured has entrusted her vehicle to the rider who had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and thereby she had breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
The 2 nd respondent has contended that, the police have filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle under Sec.3(a) and Sec.181 of M.V. Act.
In order to answer this aspect, Ex.P.4 is relevant.

A careful perusal of Ex.P.4, it appears to this Tribunal that,
the police have also charge sheeted the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 for the offence punishable under Sec.3 r/w 181 of M.V. Act also.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that, as on the date of accident, the rider of the vehicle was not possessed valid driving licence.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.4:- This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the parents of deceased Giri.
In this case, petitioners have lost their son.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth, which can never be equated in terms of the money.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency".
Hence, Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are considered as dependents of deceased.

The deceased was a bachelor, hence 1/2 of the amount is to be deducted towards personal Venkatasu vs S. Subbamma on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84083692/
6 expenses.
18. Already this Tribunal has observed that, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 18 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".
"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
19. In this case the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 18 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling, 40% of the income of Rs.15,000/- is Rs.6,000/-.

By adding the said amount with Rs.15,000/-, monthly income of deceased would be Rs.21,000/- (i.e., Rs.15,000 +
Rs.6,000/-).
In this case petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the deceased as a bachelor, 1/2 of the amount is to be deducted towards personal expenses of deceased.

After deducting 1/2 from Rs.21,000/- the actual monthly income would be Rs.10,500/-
(i.e, Rs.21,000 - Rs.10,500).

Then, total income of the deceased per annum would be Rs.1,26,000/-
(Rs.10,500 x 12).
20.
As discussed supra, the deceased was 18 years old at the time of death, the multiplier of 18 is applied, which is appropriate to age of deceased.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs.1,26,000 x 18 = Rs.22,68,000/- towards for loss of dependency.

21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

sentences.text: According to the petitioners, they have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses.
In order to substantiate the same, they have not produced any documents.
Now, the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners are also entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the petitioners are the father and mother of deceased.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.
Therefore, petitioners are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards loss of estate.

23. Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:- While answering Issue No.3, this Tribunal has come to conclusion that, the rider of offending vehicle was not possessed valid driving licence at the time of accident.
The learned counsel for the petitioners vehemently argued that, the accident occurred much earlier to amendment of Motor Vehicles Act.

Hence, though the rider of vehicle had not possessed D.L.,
liability can be fastened on the insurance company with a liberty given to them to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

In the line of her arguments, counsel for the petitioners has relied on the following decisions:
1. 2018 ACJ 2163, between Shamanna and Another Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriendal Insurance Co. Ltd., and Another.
2. 2020 ACJ 2560, between New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and Another.
3. 2021 ACJ 2165, between Ayisa and Others Vs. Manager, New India Assurance Co.
Ltd., and Another.
24.

Hence, he is not entitled for compensation from the insurance company.

In support of his line of arguments, counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in M.F.A. No.174 of 2018 C/w M.F.A.6621 of 2018, between The National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Sri. Sanaulla Khan and Others.

She also pointed out that, as per Ex.R.2, the respondent No.2,
Insurance Company has issued the package policy to the two wheeler for a period from 22.03.2019 to midnight on 21.03.2024.
Suppose if the policy issued to the said vehicle was Act Policy or Statutory policy or Liability only policy, then the risk of pillion rider is not covered.

However, in so for as Package Policy or Comprahensive Police is concerned, the risk of inmate or pillion rider is Venkatasu vs S. Subbamma on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84083692/

sentences.text: Hence, the arguments of the counsel for the respondent No.2 holds no water.
25. I have carefully gone through the decisions relied by the counsel for the petitioners.

In all the decisions, the Hon'ble Apex Court as well the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka directed the insurance company to pay the compensation and then recover the amount from the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.30131/2021 dated: 12.05.2020 between New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and Others held that, "the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the circumstances,
applying the principles of law has held in the judgments referred (Supra) "pay and recover" is to be ordered.
It is to be held that, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.

As the offending vehicle was duly covered by the policy issued by the insurer as on the date of accident,
the insurer shall satisfy the award to the claimant in the first instance and is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle".
26.

Apart from that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. and Others reported in 2018 (7) SCC 558, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held at para 24 that, "the Tribunal as well as the High Court had directed the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. and Others reported in 2018 (7) SCC 558
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swarna Singh and Others cases pertaining to pay and recovery principle".
27. In the instant case, there is no dispute with regard to the policy.
However, the respondent No.2 contended that, the risk of the pillion rider is not covered.

At the cost of repetition, as per Ex.R.2,
the insurance company has issued the package policy.

At this juncutre, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2013 (1) SCC 731, between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
Vs. Balakrishna.
The Hon'ble Apex Court differenciate the "Act Policy/Statutory Policy/Liability Only Policy and Comprehansive Policy/Package Policy".

It is held that, under the Act Policy, the injury or death occurred in respect of occupants of the Car/Jeep/vehicle and pillion rider in case of two wheeler the risk is not covered under the Act Policy.
Hence, the insurance companies are not liable to pay compensation.
But under the comprahensive policy, the injury or death occurred in respect of occupants of the Car/Jeep/vehicle and pillion rider in case of two wheeler the risk is covered.
Hence, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.

It is relevant to note that,
on careful perusal of the decision relied by the counsel for the respondent No.2, it appears to this Tribunal that, in the said case the vehicle was covered Act Only Policy.

However, in the instant case,
the insurance company has issued package policy.
Therefore, the decision relied by the respondent No.2 will not come to the aid of 2nd respondent.
28. It is relevant to note that, R.W.1 has produced insurance policy, which is marked as Ex.R.2.
Precisely, policy was in force as on the date of accident.

Hence, by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court and also the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the 2 nd respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization and further the 2 nd respondent-insurer is at liberty to recover the award amount from the 1 st respondent- R.C. owner Venkatasu vs S. 29. ISSUE No.5:- In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.23,89,000/- (Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Eighty Nine Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
It is clarified that, the insurer-2nd respondent is at liberty to recover the award amount from the 1st respondent-owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :

On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are entitled for 50% each with interest.
50% of share of petitioner Nos.1 and 2 with interest is to be paid to them through E- payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of their share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in their respective name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.

It is clarified that, the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

:: J U D G M E N T :
:
Petitioners have filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Giri in the road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to excess speed, the rider of motor cycle lost control over the vehicle and caused the accident.
The accident was occurred only due to rash or negligent riding of the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 and in this regard Gangavaram police have registered the case against the rider of above said vehicle.
The insured has knowingly entrusted the offending vehicle to the rider, who had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle.
Hence, she has breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
The police have filed charge sheet against the rider of motor cycle under Sec.3(a) and Sec.181 of M.V. Act.
This respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its validity with respect to vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 and contended that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, valid and effective driving licence of the rider of vehicle.
The offending vehicle was not involved in the accident and caused the accident.
The petitioners in collusion with the police have created false records and implicated the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 to get compensation.
The accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself and not due to negligent act of rider of the offending vehicle.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1. Whether petitioners prove that, Giri was died on 29.08.2021 due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of rider of motor cycle vehicle bearing Registration No.AP-39-S-6252 as stated in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?
3. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that, rider of the motor cycle has no valid and effective DL?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
5. What order or award?
Now, the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 or not?
Now, the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners are also entitled for consortium or not?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the rider of Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.4.
It is relevant to note that, though the respondent No.2 has contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, however, in order to substantiate the same, the 2nd respondent has not placed any material before this Tribunal.
Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S-6252 by its rider.
In the instant case, it is relevant to note that, the respondent No.2-Insurance company has not examined the rider of offending vehicle.
At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider, the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-S- 6252 ride the same in a rash or negligent manner and lost control over the said vehicle and capsized the motor cycle on the road.
Due to the said impact, the deceased Giri sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries on 01.09.2021 while taking treatment in the hospital.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that rider of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.AP- 39-S-6252 has caused the accident.
In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the age of the deceased.
On careful perusal of said document, it reveals that, the year of birth of deceased is mentioned as 2003.
The accident was occurred on 29.08.2021.
Therefore, age of the deceased is considered as 18 years at the time of accident.
15. In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2021 is Rs.15,000/- per month.
In the instant case, accident was occurred in the year 2021.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
According to respondent No.2, the insured has entrusted her vehicle to the rider who had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and thereby she had breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
The 2 nd respondent has contended that, the police have filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle under Sec.3(a) and Sec.181 of M.V. Act.
21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.
27. In the instant case, there is no dispute with regard to the policy.
The Hon'ble Apex Court differenciate the "Act Policy/Statutory Policy/Liability Only Policy and Comprehansive Policy/Package Policy".
opennyai_summary.decision:
19. In this case the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, petitioners are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards loss of estate.
The details of compensation amount is as under:
 S.No. Heads Rs.
 1. Towards loss of Rs. 22,68,000/-
 Dependency.
 2. Towards spousal and Rs. 88,000/-
 44,000 X 2  filial consortium,
 3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/-
Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.23,89,000/-.
Hence, by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court and also the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the 2 nd respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization and further the 2 nd respondent-insurer is at liberty to recover the award amount from the 1 st respondent- R.C. owner Venkatasu vs S. Subbamma on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84083692/
9 of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
Accordingly, Issue No.4 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
29. ISSUE No.5:- In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following.
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.23,89,000/- (Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Eighty Nine Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
It is clarified that, the insurer-2nd respondent is at liberty to recover the award amount from the 1st respondent-owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are entitled for 50% each with interest.
50% of share of petitioner Nos.1 and 2 with interest is to be paid to them through E- payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of their share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in their respective name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Hence, though the rider of vehicle had not possessed D.L.,
liability can be fastened on the insurance company with a liberty given to them to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
